text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000127's 99215 rate is far above expectation in every complexity tier, but the few charts returned all support the billed level, so the evidence points in different directions.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevation is not confined to sicker patients. The 99215 share runs roughly ten times the all-provider rate even among patients with zero or one chronic condition, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s carry simple-visit diagnoses such as Z09 follow-up (C0074027, C0074349, C0074389), N39.0 (C0074379, C0074509), M54.50 back pain (C0074587, C0074667) and J06.9 URI (C0074777); billing is also almost entirely 99214/99215 with very few lower codes. Against that, every documented 99215 was supported at high MDM (e.g., C0074542, C0074748, C0074842), and there is no sign of inflated data-reviewed notes on claims without a lab or test line. The key ambiguity is that only about 2% of claims have records, and with 9 documented 99215s even the comparison providers' unsupported rate would predict only about one mismatch, so zero mismatches does not clear the provider. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215s listed in the packet, especially the Z09, URI and back-pain visits, to see whether high MDM is genuinely documented or templated."}
